prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t say there’s one single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right company depends on your neighborhood, budget, whether it’s residential or commercial, and the exact problem. I can, however, help you pick a great contractor and suggest a few reputable Houston-area firms and questions to ask.

If you want me to recommend the best options for your situation, tell me your ZIP code, whether it’s a home or business, the make/model/age of your AC (if known), and whether it’s an emergency.

Quick list of well-regarded Houston HVAC companies (based on reputation and reviews as of mid‑2024; verify current ratings yourself):
- John Moore Services — long-standing local company offering AC, plumbing, electrical; large footprint in Houston.
- Baker Brothers Plumbing, AC & Electrical — Houston-based family company with strong local reviews.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (Houston) — national chain with broad service and emergency coverage.
- Holt Services — Houston-based with good local reviews for AC repair and maintenance.
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (local franchise options) — commonly used for prompt service.

How to pick the best contractor
- Licensing & certifications: technician NATE certification and EPA Section 608 certification for refrigerant handling. Ask if the company is registered with the appropriate Texas authority.
- Insurance & bonding: verify liability insurance and workers’ comp.
- Experience & specialties: ask about experience with your unit make/model and whether they do the exact repair you need.
- Reviews & references: check Google, Yelp, BBB, and recent customer reviews for speed, honesty, and follow‑through.
- Written estimate & diagnostic fee: get a written quote that lists parts, labor, permits, and warranties. Ask about diagnostic fee policy.
- Warranty & guarantees: ask about warranties on parts and labor and any satisfaction guarantees.
- Availability: emergency/after-hours service and typical response times.
- Price transparency: beware of very low bids that lack detail—get at least 2–3 estimates.

Questions to ask any HVAC company before hiring
- Are your technicians NATE certified and EPA 608 certified?
- Are you licensed/registered to work in Texas and insured?
- Can you provide a written estimate and explain all charges?
- What parts and labor warranties do you offer?
- How soon can you come, and is there an emergency fee?
- Do you perform permits and code‑compliant work?

Next steps
- If you share your ZIP code and AC problem/symptoms (won’t turn on, short-cycling, weak airflow, leaking, strange noises, age), I can narrow the list to top-rated local options and give a plan (diagnostic questions, estimated cost ranges, and what to expect).

Would you like me to find a few top-rated companies for your ZIP code and pull up recent reviews?
